title: STRANGE MINUTE · WHAT IF #8

lines.text: What if you fell into Jupiter?
First surprise: there's no ground to land on.
Jupiter is a giant ball of gas. And it pulls hard.
Its gravity is about two and a half times Earth's.
We know what happens, because NASA tried it.
In 1995, the Galileo probe dove in.
lines.say: In nineteen ninety-five, the Galileo probe dove in.

lines.text: It hit the air at about 106,000 miles per hour.
lines.say: It hit the air at about a hundred and six thousand miles per hour.

lines.text: Its heat shield blazed past 28,000 degrees.
lines.say: Its heat shield blazed past twenty-eight thousand degrees.

lines.text: Then you'd sink through clouds of ammonia ice.
Past a storm bigger than the whole Earth.
The pressure keeps squeezing harder and harder.
Galileo sent data for 58 minutes. Then silence.
lines.say: Galileo sent data for fifty-eight minutes. Then silence.

lines.text: The strange part? Deep down, hydrogen turns into liquid metal.
You'd never hit the bottom. You'd become part of Jupiter.
So, would you still take the fall?
